record.title: LiLiCorr correlates parallel draft marginals for faster speculative decoding
record.summary: NVIDIA Nemotron researchers published LiLiCorr, a speculative-decoding method that correlates per-position marginals from parallel drafts in one network pass and turns coherence modeling into matrix operations.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report LiLiCorr as the fastest system in almost all evaluated benchmark/concurrency/input-length settings.

engineering_implications: Potentially useful as a minimum speculative-serving baseline for MTP-capable models.

evidence_gaps.description: Full paper/code and exact matched-control accounting have not yet been audited in this record.

limitations: The current Observatory record has not yet reconstructed every matched baseline, acceptance-rate detail or kernel configuration from the full paper/artifacts.
research_implications: Correlation-aware parallel drafting may improve the acceptance/parallelism tradeoff without requiring autoregressive draft generation.
brief.summary: NVIDIA Nemotron researchers published LiLiCorr, a speculative-decoding method that correlates per-position marginals from parallel drafts in one network pass and turns coherence modeling into matrix operations.

technical.claimed_result: The authors position LiLiCorr as a broadly faster speculative-decoding system than evaluated alternatives.
technical.compute_or_cost: Designed to preserve drafter parallelism while improving proposal coherence/acceptance efficiency.
technical.demonstrated_result: NVIDIA reports evaluation across benchmarks, serving concurrencies and input lengths, with LiLiCorr fastest in almost all evaluated settings.
technical.implementation_status: Research project publicly announced; artifact completeness requires follow-up.
technical.mechanism: Correlates per-position marginals from a parallel block drafter in a single pass, expressing draft coherence through parallelizable matrix operations.
technical.novelty: Adds lightweight correlation structure to otherwise independent parallel draft marginals.
technical.regime: Inference-time speculative decoding across multiple serving concurrencies and prompt lengths.
technical.reproducibility: Primary project description is public; full independent reproduction remains open.
technical.strongest_baseline: Parallel block drafting and contemporary speculative-decoding systems evaluated by the authors.

brief.title: LiLiCorr correlates parallel draft marginals for faster speculative decoding
brief.why_it_matters: It targets the core weakness of parallel block drafters—independent token marginals—without giving up their parallelism, making it directly relevant to high-throughput multi-token prediction and speculative serving.
